title: Lesson 3: Close Read-aloud, Session 2: What Makes Day and Night
objective: Students will distinguish information learned from illustrations and text in an informational book to describe the pattern of light and dark on earth and record observations about the sun and moon using descriptive words.

what_is_taught.skill: distinguish information learned from illustrations and text
describe the pattern of light and dark on earth
identify adjectives that describe the sun, moon, and stars
use adjectives to describe objects orally
participate in a close read-aloud of an informational text
engage in partner discussion using sentence frames
use a speaking and listening protocol to share ideas
record observations using pictures and words during shared writing
formulate complete sentences using descriptive words

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify adjectives and information from text and illustrations
student_actions.oral_production: respond orally to questions and participate in partner discussions using sentence frames
student_actions.written_production: participate in shared writing by contributing words and ideas
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain meanings of words and describe observations orally
student_actions.comprehension_response: answer questions about text and illustrations orally

evidence.quote: 'Why did we circle/highlight some of the words in the poem?' (We circled the adjectives.)
'What were some adjectives that we circled to describe the sun?' (orange, round)

'As I reread the poem today, I want you to listen for adjectives used to describe the sun, moon, and stars. When you hear an adjective read aloud, quietly put a thumb out in front of your chest.' Model the hand gesture if necessary.
Read aloud poem, fluently and with expression.
'What were some adjectives that you heard to describe the sun, moon, or stars?' (sun: hot, moon: full, stars: twinkling)
'What is something at home or at school that we could describe using this adjective?' (a bowl of soup; the nightlight)

Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner: 'What does this learning target mean?' (find information that is different in the illustrations and in the text to tell about the pattern of light and dark on earth)
Guide students through the close read-aloud for What Makes Day and Night using the Close Read-aloud Guide: What Makes Day and Night (Session 2; for teacher reference).

To activate background knowledge of familiar concepts and support comprehension of vocabulary, invite students to recall a time they sat in a shadow outside (e.g., under a tree, in the shade of a building, etc.) as the Word Wall card for shadow is added to the Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall.
Model standing and rotating in place for students. While rotating, say: 'I am rotating right now.'
'What are some words to describe what I am doing?' (turning, spinning, rotating)
'What does it mean to rotate?' (turn in a circle around a center point)
Play the 'Blue Marble Animations' video.
Guide students through Round 1 of the protocol using the following question:
Provide a sentence frame as necessary:
Refocus students whole group.
'How would you describe the sun in this photograph? What adjectives could you use to describe it?' (yellow, hidden)
'How would you describe the moon in this photograph? What adjectives could you use to describe it?' (sliver, white)
Display the Describing the Sun and Moon recording form.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group.
'What does the sun look like?'

As students share responses, use their ideas to complete page 1. Think aloud how to use the words from the question itself as a cue to formulate the answer using a complete sentence. (Example: The sun looks yellow and hidden.)
Draw a quick sketch of what the sun looks like.
Point to the question on page 2 and read it aloud:

As students share responses, use their ideas to complete page 2. Think aloud how to use the words from the question itself as a cue to formulate the answer using a complete sentence. (Example: The moon looks white and little.)
Draw a quick sketch of what the moon looks like.

For ELLs: Support students as they formulate sentences for the Describing the Sun and Moon recording form. Invite students to use the Adjectives Construction board (See Lesson 2) with the sentence frame: 'The [sun/moon] looks like a(n) [adjective] [noun].' (Example: The sun looks like an orange ball. The sun looks bright and yellow.) Invite students to identify any new adjectives they might like to add to the board.

Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner: 'What is something you learned from an illustration to describe the pattern of light and dark on earth?' (I saw a picture of the earth spinning. Half of the earth faces the sun, and the other half faces away from the sun.)
'What did you read in the text that confirmed what you saw in the illustration?' (The text said that the earth spins around and light from the sun falls on one-half of the spinning earth.)

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model fluent expressive reading of the poem and the close read-aloud text; model standing and rotating to demonstrate earth's rotation; model shared writing by thinking aloud and sketching observations; model use of sentence frames for partner discussions and descriptive sentences.

scope.breadth: Focus on distinguishing information from illustrations and text about earth's light and dark pattern and describing the sun and moon using adjectives.
scope.depth: Includes comprehension of informational text, vocabulary development, oral language practice, and shared writing.

sections_covered.warm_up: Engaging the Learner: 'What We See: The Sun, Moon, and Stars' Poem
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Close Read-aloud, Session 2: What Makes Day and Night, Pages 14-15
sections_covered.independent_application: Shared Writing: Describing the Sun and Moon

supports.english_language_learners: Encourage use of sentence frames and the Adjectives Construction board; provide picture and word cues; model language structures.
supports.universal_design_udl: Use total participation techniques; provide sentence frames; use visual supports such as photographs, word walls, and anchor charts.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Use sentence frames and word banks to support oral and written expression.
supports.above_level_extend: Challenge students to add details during partner discussions and share out with evidence from text and illustrations.

assessment.method: Observation of student oral responses, partner discussions, and participation in shared writing.
assessment.recognition_vs_production: Primarily production through oral and written responses.
